One player gives a clue, everyone else guesses the description for it.

What number is the best fit
Answer: Seven - A weird plastic musician
Place the game grid in the centre of the table
Each cell in the grid corresponds to two description cards. For example,
box 8 corresponds to a good, wide animal.
Draw a random theme card, and as a group select a side
and place them on the top left of the board
and place them on the top right of the board
Give each player a set of cards 1-9
Pick a player to be the Clue Giver. They shuffle their cards 1-9, pick one
at random, and keep it secret.
The Clue Giver now thinks of a clue that fits the theme and the two
descriptions. Don't worry about giving a perfect clue, they don't exist!
What counts as a clue? That's up to the group. It's typically one person
or thing. A potato. Issac Newton. Goat's cheese pizza. Just don't use a
Every other player now needs to work out what on earth they might
mean. When you've worked out the Clue Giver's number (or guessed),
place the corresponding card face down in front of you.
When all players have chosen, flip the cards and reveal your guesses.
The Clue Giver then reveals their number, and you see who was right.
Once you've revealed the answer, the clue's two descriptions change.
Swap them out for new description cards.
After all players have given a clue for the theme (or you fancy a change),
swap out the theme. Draw a new random theme card, and as a group
decide which side to use for the next round.
The only limit to the number of players is the number of selection cards.
If you want to play with more than 6 people, players can hold up a
number of fingers 1-9, or write their guesses down on a piece of paper.
In Angry Yellow Fruit, each player that guessed correctly gets a point.
The Clue Giver gets a point for each player that got it right.
